questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true for dry heat method of sterilisation?

options.A: Usually sterilisation is done by heating at a temperature of $160^\circ\text{C}$ for two hours
options.B: Destruction of microorganism is effected by oxidation of essential cell constituents
options.C: This method is not suitable for powders and oily materials
options.D: This method is not suitable for surgical dressings

questions.explanation: Dry heat is actually very suitable for heat-stable powders and oily materials.

questions.question_text: Enteric coating is given to tablets in order to

options.A: Protect the medicament from atmospheric effects
options.B: Ensure highest concentration of drug in the intestine
options.C: Separate chemical or physical incompatible ingredients
options.D: Prolong the duration of action of medicaments

questions.explanation: Enteric coating resists gastric fluid and disintegrates in the intestine, ensuring drug release there.

questions.question_text: If a capsule is numbered as 000 which means

options.A: It is the smallest sized capsule with a capacity of 100 mg
options.B: It is for the inclusion of ophthalmic ointments only
options.C: The shape of the capsule is oval
options.D: It is the largest sized and for veterinary purpose only

questions.explanation: 000 is the largest standard capsule size used mainly for veterinary or bulk filling purposes.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a correct statement regarding soft gelatin capsule?

options.A: Soft gelatin shells may contain methyl and propyl parabens as preservative
options.B: Not suitable for use as suppositories
options.D: The manufacturing and filling of medicaments are done in separate operations

questions.explanation: Preservatives like methyl and propyl parabens are commonly added to soft gelatin shell formulations to prevent microbial growth.

questions.question_text: For the evaluation of tablet, a test used to measure the amount of time required for the drug substance in tablet to go into solution under specified condition is known as
questions.explanation: Dissolution test measures the rate and extent of drug substance going into solution.

questions.question_text: Unequal distribution of colour on a tablet with light and dark areas standing out in a uniform surface is known as
questions.explanation: Mottling is the term for unequal color distribution on a tablet surface.

questions.question_text: Mechanism of killing microorganisms by gaseous sterilisation is
questions.explanation: Gaseous sterilizing agents like ethylene oxide act via alkylation of cellular proteins and nucleic acids.

questions.question_text: Role of Glycerin or sorbitol in the manufacturing of capsule shell as
questions.explanation: Glycerin and sorbitol act as plasticizers to render the gelatin shell flexible and elastic.

questions.question_text: Sterilisation by heating with a bactericide

options.A: Can be used safely for intrathecal injections
options.B: Not suitable for intravenous injection when single dose exceeds 15 ml
options.C: Is performed before the preparation is transferred into the final container

questions.explanation: Heating with a bactericide is restricted for large volume intravenous injections (exceeding 15 ml) due to toxicity risks from the bactericide.

questions.question_text: During the formulation of tablet the purpose of adding magnesium stearate as
questions.explanation: Magnesium stearate is widely used as a tablet and capsule lubricant to prevent adhesion to compression equipment.

questions.question_text: Lugol's solution is
questions.explanation: Lugol's solution is an aqueous solution of iodine and potassium iodide.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a common ingredient in ear drops as dewaxing agent?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide releases oxygen and helps soften and loosen earwax.

questions.question_text: Penicillamine is an antidote used in the poisoning of
questions.explanation: Penicillamine is a chelating agent used to treat copper (Wilson's disease) and lead poisoning.

questions.question_text: An oxidative antimicrobial agent is
questions.explanation: Sodium hypochlorite exerts its antimicrobial effect primarily through oxidation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding ammonium chloride?

options.A: It is an irritating expectorant and used as an ingredient in cough mixtures
options.B: Given to aid easy elimination in lead poisoning
options.C: In the liver it is metabolised into urea
options.D: It is used as a systemic alkaliniser

questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is an acidifying agent, not an alkaliniser, as it dissociates into hydrogen and chloride ions.

questions.question_text: which one of the following is used for the treatment of schistosomiasis (Kala-azar) and administered intravenously?
questions.explanation: Antimony potassium tartrate (tartar emetic) has historically been used for schistosomiasis.

questions.question_text: A sulphur compound which is a common ingredient in shampoos and lotions for the treatment of dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis
questions.explanation: Selenium sulfide is widely used in anti-dandruff shampoos.

questions.question_text: Green vitriol is
questions.explanation: Green vitriol is the common name for hydrated ferrous sulfate.

questions.question_text: Prolonged use of silver preparation may lead to a condition known as
questions.explanation: Argyria is a condition caused by prolonged exposure to silver preparations, characterized by blue-gray skin discoloration.

questions.question_text: An organic mercury compound which is commonly used as antiseptic/antifungal agent is
questions.explanation: Thiomersal (thimerosal) is an organomercury compound used as an antiseptic and antifungal agent.

questions.question_text: Viscosity builders used in Ophthalmic formulation
questions.explanation: Carboxymethyl cellulose is commonly used as a viscosity-imparting agent in eye drops to increase retention time.

questions.question_text: Thickening of a shampoo may be carried by addition of
questions.explanation: Carboxy vinyl polymers (carbomers) are widely used thickening agents in cosmetics and shampoos.

questions.question_text: Eye Ointment base should melt at
questions.explanation: Eye ointment bases must melt or soften at body temperature to ensure proper drug release and avoid irritation.

questions.question_text: For preparation of emulsions using fixed oil the ratio of oil: water : Gum
questions.explanation: The standard primary emulsion ratio for fixed oils using gum acacia is 4:2:1 (Oil:Water:Gum).

questions.question_text: Suspensions are biphasic liquid dosage form of medicament in which the finely divided solid particles ranging from
questions.explanation: Suspended solid particles in pharmaceutical suspensions typically range between 0.5 to 5.0 microns.

questions.question_text: Example for semi-synthetic thickening agents in suspension
questions.explanation: Microcrystalline cellulose is a semi-synthetic cellulose derivative used as a suspending and thickening agent.

questions.question_text: Which among the ingredients is used for the preparation of concentrated Haemodialysis fluid B.P.C.?
questions.explanation: Sodium acetate is commonly used as a buffer source in haemodialysis fluids.

questions.question_text: Examples of liquid Anti perspirants
questions.explanation: Aluminium chlorohydrate is widely used as an active antiperspirant ingredient.

questions.question_text: Hair remover is otherwise called
questions.explanation: Chemical hair removers are known as depilatories.

questions.question_text: Rubber closures are washed with hot solution of
questions.explanation: Rubber closures are typically washed with a 0.2% sodium pyrophosphate solution to remove surface impurities.

questions.question_text: Vasaka contains _________ % w/w of vasicine calculated on the dried basis
questions.explanation: Vasaka (Adhatoda vasica) contains not less than 0.5% vasicine on a dried basis according to pharmacopeial standards.

questions.question_text: Tulsi comes under category
questions.explanation: Ocimum sanctum (Tulsi) is well known for its immunomodulatory properties.

questions.question_text: Peppermint oil is obtained by
questions.explanation: Volatile oils like peppermint oil are typically extracted using steam distillation.

questions.question_text: Powdered ergot when treated with ________ solution develops strong odour of trimethylamine
questions.explanation: Treatment of ergot with sodium hydroxide releases free trimethylamine, producing a characteristic strong fishy odor.

questions.question_text: Terminalia Arjuna is used as
questions.explanation: Terminalia arjuna bark is traditionally used in indigenous systems of medicine for cardiovascular diseases and liver disorders including jaundice.

questions.question_text: Active constituent of Rhubarb
questions.explanation: Rhubarb contains anthraquinone derivatives such as rhein, emodin, and chrysophanol.

questions.question_text: Anti-sweetening agent in Gymnema sylvestre
questions.explanation: Gymnemic acids are the active anti-sweetening principles found in the leaves of Gymnema sylvestre.

questions.question_text: Ergotoxine test gives __________ colour
questions.explanation: Ergot alkaloids give a characteristic deep purple or blue-violet color with p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde (Van Urk's reagent).

questions.question_text: Triphala and chyavanprash contain
questions.explanation: Amla (Emblica officinalis) is a primary ingredient in both Triphala and Chyavanprash.

questions.question_text: Main triglycerides in castor oil
questions.explanation: Castor oil consists mainly of tricinolein, which is the triglyceride of ricinoleic acid.

questions.question_text: The antiseptic which is an acridine derivative
questions.explanation: Proflavine is an antiseptic acridine dye derivative.

questions.question_text: Co-trimoxazole contains sulphamethoxazole and trimethoprim in the ratio
questions.explanation: Co-trimoxazole formulation standardly combines sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim in a 5:1 ratio (e.g., 400 mg sulfamethoxazole to 80 mg trimethoprim).

questions.question_text: The heterocyclic system present in isoniazid
questions.explanation: Isoniazid is the hydrazide of isonicotinic acid, containing a pyridine ring.

questions.question_text: The Penicillin which has an isoxazole ring in its structure
questions.explanation: Cloxacillin belongs to the isoxazolyl penicillin group containing an isoxazole ring.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is a butyrophenone derivative?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol is a classic antipsychotic drug of the butyrophenone chemical class.

questions.question_text: A tricyclic antidepressant which belongs to the category of dibenzocycloheptenes
questions.explanation: Amitriptyline is a dibenzocycloheptene derivative tricyclic antidepressant.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is a non-catecholamine?
questions.explanation: Terbutaline, phenylephrine, and ephedrine all lack the 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl structure characteristic of catecholamines.

questions.question_text: A synthetic anticholinergic drug which is an ester carrying xanthene heterocycle
questions.explanation: Propantheline is a synthetic quaternary ammonium compound containing a xanthene ester moiety.

questions.question_text: 4-Chloro – N – furfuryl – 5-sulphamoyl anthranilic acid is
questions.explanation: The chemical name 4-chloro-N-furfuryl-5-sulfamoylanthranilic acid corresponds to frusemide (furosemide).

questions.question_text: An antineoplastic agent which is a pyrimidine analogue is
questions.explanation: Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a pyrimidine analogue antineoplastic drug.

questions.question_text: The ratio of Carbidopa–Levodopa combination used in the treatment of parkinsonism is
questions.explanation: Carbidopa and Levodopa are commonly combined in fixed ratios such as 1:4 or 1:10, depending on the formulation.

questions.question_text: Respiratory depression due to morphine overdose can be reversed by
questions.explanation: Naloxone is an opioid receptor antagonist used to reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression.

questions.question_text: Myasthenia gravis, a chronic neuromuscular disease is diagnosed by intravenous injection of
questions.explanation: Edrophonium test (Tensilon test) uses short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor edrophonium to diagnose myasthenia gravis.

questions.question_text: A prostaglandin derivative used in the treatment of glaucoma is
questions.explanation: Bimatoprost is a prostamide analog used topically to treat glaucoma and ocular hypertension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug is a Serotonin-2 (5 HT 2) antagonist?
questions.explanation: Methysergide is an ergot alkaloid derivative that acts as a 5-HT2 receptor antagonist.

questions.question_text: An antihypertensive drug which is not an arteriolar vasodialator
questions.explanation: Methyldopa is a centrally acting sympatholytic antihypertensive, whereas hydralazine, minoxidil, and diazoxide are direct arteriolar vasodilators.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an antiretroviral drug?
questions.explanation: Zidovudine (AZT) is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used as an antiretroviral against HIV.

questions.question_text: An oral hypoglycemic agent, which comes under the category of second-generation sulphonyl urea is
questions.explanation: Glibenclamide (glyburide) is a second-generation sulfonylurea.

questions.question_text: The antibiotic which binds to 30S subunit of the bacterial ribosome and inhibit protein synthesis
questions.explanation: Doxycycline is a tetracycline antibiotic that binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit.

questions.question_text: A selective Beta I antagonist
questions.explanation: Atenolol is a cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic antagonist.

questions.question_text: Which schedule specifies the retailer to keep a copy of the prescription for two years while selling certain class of drugs?
questions.explanation: Under Indian Pharmacy regulations, Schedule H drugs require prescriptions to be retained for two years.

questions.question_text: The latest amendment of Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940, and Rules 1945 is upto
questions.explanation: Standard editions frequently reference updates up to December 31, 2017 in recent academic exam compendiums.

questions.question_text: Good laboratory practices and requirements of premises and equipment is specified in
questions.explanation: Schedule L-1 prescribes the Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) and requirements for premises and equipment.

questions.question_text: As per the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act-1954, which of the diseases, disorder or condition cannot be claimed to be cured?
questions.explanation: All listed conditions are prohibited from being advertised as cured under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act.

questions.question_text: The register of pharmacists also known as the Central Register as per the Pharmacy Act-1948 contains

options.A: Names of all persons for the time being entered in the register for a State

questions.explanation: The Central Register contains names from state registers and is considered a public document under the law.

questions.question_text: Manufacturer of cosmetics to conform to the latest Bureau of Indian Standards requirements is specified in
questions.explanation: Schedule S outlines the standards for cosmetic products and adherence to Bureau of Indian Standards.

questions.question_text: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act was enacted in the year
questions.explanation: The NDPS Act was enacted by the Parliament of India in 1985.

questions.question_text: The number of registered pharmacists nominated by respective state government in a state council is
questions.explanation: State pharmacy councils include 5 members nominated by the state government.

questions.question_text: Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 is punishable up to the maximum imprisonment of
questions.explanation: First-time conviction under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act carries imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both, but subsequent offenses carry up to two years.

questions.question_text: Good manufacturing practices for Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani medicines is specified in
questions.explanation: Schedule T outlines GMP requirements for Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani drugs.

questions.question_text: One among the below is not an objective of sales promotion
questions.explanation: Prize contests are a tool or technique of sales promotion rather than its ultimate fundamental objective.

questions.question_text: The science to examine and check the accuracy of the recorded transactions is called
questions.explanation: Accountancy encompasses the rules and systematic examination of recorded financial transactions.

questions.question_text: Reference check of the personnel is the process under
questions.explanation: Reference checks are conducted as part of the personnel recruitment and selection process.

questions.question_text: A Co-operative society is required to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act.
questions.explanation: Co-operative societies in India are commonly registered under the Co-operative Societies Act of 1912.

questions.question_text: An industry manufacturing a chemical by a standardized chemical reaction is called
questions.explanation: Synthetic industries manufacture new products by combining materials via chemical reactions.

questions.question_text: If a customer is allowed to draw cheques even if there is no balance in his account is called
questions.explanation: An overdraft facility allows account holders to withdraw money exceeding their account balance.

questions.question_text: Which type of cash book is needed to receive or allow cash discount in a business transactions?
questions.explanation: A three-column cash book includes columns for cash, bank, and discount.

questions.question_text: The sum of money or goods withdrawn by the proprietor from business for his personal use is called
questions.explanation: Withdrawals of cash or goods by the owner for personal use are termed drawings.

questions.question_text: The loan sanctioned against the pledge of the property of the company is called
questions.explanation: A mortgage is a loan secured against immovable property assets.

questions.question_text: ABC analysis is used to
questions.explanation: ABC analysis classifies inventory items based on their consumption value or annual usage.

questions.question_text: Ryles tube is used for

options.C: Nutritional support and aspiration of stomach content

questions.explanation: A Ryles tube (nasogastric tube) is passed through the nose into the stomach for feeding or gastric aspiration.

questions.question_text: Method for monitoring particulate matter in parenteral products
questions.explanation: Visual inspection is the standard method used for detecting visible particulate matter in parenteral preparations.

questions.question_text: Pore size of membrane filter used in test for sterility
questions.explanation: Pharmacopeial standards specify a nominal pore size of not greater than 0.45 micrometers for membrane filters used in sterility testing.

questions.question_text: The guidelines for inclusion or non-inclusion of drugs in the hospital formulary are framed by
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee is responsible for developing, managing, and updating the hospital formulary.

questions.question_text: Computer based system of the U.S., National Library of Medicine (NLM) that allows rapid access to store biomedical information
questions.explanation: MEDLARS (Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System) is the computerized bibliographic retrieval system developed by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

questions.question_text: New England Journal of Medicine is which type of drug information resource?
questions.explanation: Peer-reviewed medical journals like the New England Journal of Medicine publish original research and clinical studies, making them primary literature sources.

questions.question_text: Thermo labile powders are sterilized by
questions.explanation: Ethylene oxide gas is a chemical sterilization method suitable for heat-sensitive (thermolabile) powders and medical devices.

questions.question_text:
Following statements of unit dose system are correct
(i) Patient receives improved service round the clock and charged for only administered doses
(ii) Allowing nurses more time for direct patient care
(iii) Medication errors are decreased
(iv) Eliminates wastage of drugs and pilferage
questions.explanation: All listed statements accurately describe the distinct advantages of a well-implemented unit dose drug distribution system in hospitals.

questions.question_text:
All of the following statements about parenteral products are true EXCEPT
(i) The drug product is easier to remove from vials than ampule.
(ii) Ampules are intended for multiple use
(iii) Large volume parenterals are infusion solutions.
questions.explanation: Statement (ii) is false because ampules are strictly single-use containers; statement (i) is true since vials allow easier withdrawal via syringe compared to breaking ampules.

questions.question_text: In A, B, C analysis of inventory control, "A class" items are about ____ of the total items in number and nearly ____ of the annual consumption value of the items
questions.explanation: ABC analysis follows the Pareto principle where 'A' class items constitute about 15-20% of items and account for roughly 70-80% of the inventory value.

questions.question_text: Teratogenic drugs, EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Dicyclomine is an anticholinergic used for gastrointestinal cramps and is not a recognized teratogen, whereas diethylstilbestrol, warfarin, and phenytoin are established teratogens.

questions.question_text: The international drug monitoring centre is at
questions.explanation: The Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) in Sweden serves as the WHO collaborating centre for international drug monitoring.

questions.question_text: Which of the following organisms can cause peptic ulcer disease?
questions.explanation: Helicobacter pylori is a gram-negative bacterium strongly associated with the pathogenesis of peptic ulcer disease and gastritis.

questions.question_text: The term coronary artery disease is used to designate all of the following conditions, EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Congestive Heart Failure is a clinical syndrome resulting from various cardiac dysfunctions, whereas angina, myocardial infarction, and sudden cardiac death are direct manifestations of coronary artery disease.

questions.question_text: Normal safety range of potassium in adult blood is
questions.explanation: The normal physiological serum potassium concentration range in healthy adult blood is approximately $3.5 - 5.0\text{ mEq/L}$.

questions.question_text: Burton's line is a clinical sign found in patients with chronic poisoning of
questions.explanation: Burton's line (a bluish-purple pigmentation on the gums) is a classic clinical indicator of chronic lead poisoning.

questions.question_text: Metabolic acidosis can be compacted by
questions.explanation: Trisaminomethane (THAM) is an alkalinizing agent used to buffer and correct metabolic acidosis.

questions.question_text: Warfarin-Metronidazole drug interaction is due to
questions.explanation: Metronidazole inhibits the hepatic metabolism (specifically CYP2C9) of S-warfarin, leading to increased anticoagulant effects and bleeding risk.

questions.question_text:
Bioavailability may be determined by using
(i) Plasma drug concentration verses time profile
(ii) Urinary drug excretion studies
(iii) Measurement of an acute pharmacological effect
(iv) Clinical studies or in-vitro studies
questions.explanation: Bioavailability can be assessed using pharmacokinetic methods (plasma and urine data) as well as pharmacodynamic and clinical study approaches.

questions.question_text:
Following statements concerning drug addition are correct EXCEPT
(i) An overpowering desire or compulsion to continue taking the drug and to obtain it by any means
(ii) A tendency to decrease the dose
(iii) Psychic/physical dependence on the effect of the drugs
questions.explanation: Drug addiction typically involves tolerance, leading to a tendency to *increase* the dose, making statement (ii) incorrect.
